leads.note: Singapore reached its target of 10 total trees this pass (7 already published + 3 shipped: sgp_008 Bodhi Tree of Pearl's Hill, sgp_009 Banyan of Tiong Bahru Park, sgp_010 Earpod Tree of Fort Canning). The remaining ~147 unique register candidates (of 163 within 5km, after removing 13 rows that matched already-published trees by coordinate) were not individually verified this pass, per the brief's 'no more than 10 total' instruction. Listed below are the strongest-looking clusters for a future deepening pass, not individually fetched/verified.

candidates: HT 2016-274 Mango, Chay Yan St State Land
HT 2003-89 Binjai (Mangifera caesia), Spottiswoode Park Road opposite Spottiswoode Apartments
HT 2013-204 already shipped as sgp_009 (Tiong Bahru Park)
HT 2005-145 Pukul Lima (Rain Tree), Everton Road top of slope opposite Block 10 carpark
HT 2012-203 Indian Rubber Tree, Duxton Plain Park near Pinnacle block 1D
HT 2003-107 Rain Tree, top of slope at junction of Spottiswoode Park Road
HT 2003-111 Pukul Lima, Kim Yam Road Stateland beside Gambier Court condominium
leads.reason: Not evidence-rejected, simply not reached: this pass verified 3 trees and stopped at the city's target of 10. HT 2005-145 and HT 2003-107 are both Samanea saman (Rain Tree / Pukul Lima are the same species under English and Malay names) roughly 65m apart at different named locations (Everton Road vs. Spottiswoode Park Road junction); a future pass should check whether these read as one tree seen from two descriptions or two genuinely separate trees before shipping both, per the register-twin rule.

Most remaining Fort Canning register rows duplicate species already represented on the page; Sea Beam/Merbatu and Bacang would add real diversity if a future pass wants to deepen this single park further.
